title: Article 141 — Law declared by Supreme Court to be binding on all courts

content.overview: Article 141 provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.
content.glance: Law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts in India.
content.study:
Article 141 is the constitutional foundation of the doctrine of precedent (stare decisis) for Supreme Court declarations of law. All courts in India are bound by the law declared by the SC. The SC itself may overrule or depart from its prior decisions in appropriate cases; subordinate courts may not.

Examination: binding on all courts; SC may reconsider its own view; ratio vs obiter (doctrinal distinction in application).

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: The law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the effect of Article 141?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 141 provides that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India. It is the constitutional basis for the binding force of Supreme Court precedent on all other courts.

examTips: SC law binds all courts in India.

keyTakeaways: Art 141: law declared by SC binding on all courts in India.
